title: Coordinate-ring identities for affine groupoid composition
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ define a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], with $c(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha\circ\beta$. Put $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$ and $\varepsilon=e^\sharp:B\to A$. Give the first factor of $D=B\otimes_{\sigma,A,\tau}B$ its $A$-structure through $\sigma$ and the second through $\tau$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with the tensor-product ring structure [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Then $R\times_{s,U,t}R\cong\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections dual to $p_0(b)=b\otimes1$ and $p_1(b)=1\otimes b$. Under this identification put $\Delta=c^\sharp:B\to D$. These ring maps satisfy $\varepsilon\sigma=\varepsilon\tau=\mathrm{id}_A$, $p_0\sigma=p_1\tau$, $\Delta\sigma=p_1\sigma$, and $\Delta\tau=p_0\tau$. In particular $\sigma,\tau$ are injective. The set $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$ is a unital subring, and the restrictions of $\sigma$ and $\tau$ to $C$ coincide.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with base ring $A$, first algebra the copy of $B$ with structure map $\sigma$, and second algebra the copy with structure map $\tau$. Supply these two algebra structures explicitly to Mathlib pullbackSpecIso. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $s=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ and $t=\operatorname{Spec}(\tau)$; transport the pullback along these equalities to obtain $F:R\times_{s,U,t}R\cong\operatorname{Spec}D$. The projection formulas for pullbackSpecIso give $F^{-1}q_0=\operatorname{Spec}(p_0)$ and $F^{-1}q_1=\operatorname{Spec}(p_1)$. Precompose the defining pullback equality $s q_0=t q_1$ by $F^{-1}$, substitute the projection formulas, and use contravariant functoriality and faithfulness of Spec to obtain $p_0\sigma=p_1\tau$.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, displayed formula and its proof; applied with the two specified A-algebra structures.

proof.text: By [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], $s\circ e=t\circ e=\mathrm{id}_U$. The contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] sends these equations to $e^\sharp\circ s^\sharp=e^\sharp\circ t^\sharp=\mathrm{id}_A$, that is, $\varepsilon\sigma=\varepsilon\tau=\mathrm{id}_A$. If $\sigma(a)=\sigma(a^{\prime})$, applying $\varepsilon$ gives $a=a^{\prime}$; the identical argument for $\tau$ proves that both maps are injective.

source.place: Tag 0231, definition-groupoid, following paragraph: e is a section of both s and t; Tag 03C8, lemma-basis, coordinate-ring notation.

proof.text: Let $q_0,q_1$ be the two projections of the composable-pair scheme, identified in step 1. The convention $c(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha\circ\beta$ gives $s\circ c=s\circ q_1$ and $t\circ c=t\circ q_0$ in [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. By the contravariant functoriality of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $q_j^\sharp=p_j$, these become $c^\sharp\circ s^\sharp=p_1\circ s^\sharp$ and $c^\sharp\circ t^\sharp=p_0\circ t^\sharp$. Setting $\Delta=c^\sharp$ proves $\Delta\sigma=p_1\sigma$ and $\Delta\tau=p_0\tau$.

source.place: Tag 02YE, lemma-diagram, commutativity of the lower-right square and top triangle; Tag 03C8, lemma-basis, first diagram.

proof.text: Since $\sigma,\tau$ are unital ring homomorphisms, $0,1\in C$. If $a,b\in C$, then $\sigma(a-b)=\sigma(a)-\sigma(b)=\tau(a)-\tau(b)=\tau(a-b)$ and $\sigma(ab)=\sigma(a)\sigma(b)=\tau(a)\tau(b)=\tau(ab)$. Thus $C$ is a unital subring of $A$. For each $a\in C$, the equality $\sigma(a)=\tau(a)$ is its defining condition, so the restrictions to $C$ coincide.
